title: NGC 6503
caption: The galaxy NGC 6503, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 6503 · constellation Draco · about 18 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This Hubble image shows the galaxy NGC 6503, which lies about 18 million light-years away in the constellation Draco. It is classed as a spiral galaxy and as a dwarf, smaller than giants like the Milky Way.

What makes NGC 6503 unusual is its surroundings. It sits at the edge of a strangely empty region of space called the Local Void. Galaxies across the Universe are arranged in a web of clusters and filaments, and voids are the large gaps in between, where very few galaxies are found.

This newer view shows a very rich set of colours that adds detail to earlier images of the galaxy. It combines filters from the ultraviolet, through visible light, and into the near-infrared, along with one that isolates the glow of hydrogen gas, often a sign of star-forming regions.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.68 x 2.24 arcminutes) and distance (18 million light years), the frame spans roughly 14,000 × 12,000 light-years. Its light set out about 18 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image combines Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys and Wide Field Camera 3, using filters from the ultraviolet to the near-infrared, plus H-alpha for glowing hydrogen. The packet does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Ultraviolet and near-infrared light are invisible to the eye, so this image records far more than a human observer could see.
